programmes.label: Bachelor Clinical Technology at Delft University of Technology, Leiden University and Erasmus University Rotterdam

exception.reason: Clinical Technology is an integrated medical-engineering and clinical-practice degree. Its compulsory spine combines organ-system medicine with biomechanics, thermodynamics, waves, biomedical instrumentation, signals, imaging, medical-image processing, bioinformatics, computer simulation and medical-technology design, alongside three levels of clinical skills and safety, a healthcare placement, complex diagnosis–therapy training and a 15-EC clinical-technology research project. UCR has meaningful biomedical science, anatomy, physiology, pathology, pharmacology, laboratory, mathematics, data, imaging and robotics courses. It does not have the required physics and biomedical-engineering progression, biomedical instrumentation laboratories, integrated organ-system engineering modules, clinical skills and safety training, supervised patient-facing placement, medical-device practice, or diagnosis-and-treatment formation. Combining UCR's biomedical and computational courses would create a strong health-and-data liberal-arts programme, but it would not be a defensible Clinical Technology comparator.
exception.curriculumContext: The official module map accounts for the full 180 EC: 60 EC in each year. Year one integrates systems biology and organ systems with mathematics, programming, biomechanics, thermodynamics, signals, biomedical instrumentation, statistics, skills and safety, and academic formation. Year two advances imaging, waves, biomechanics, bioinformatics, image processing, instrumentation, healthcare information, medical-technology design, clinical skills and a healthcare placement. Year three combines a 15-EC minor with intensive-care simulation, bioinformatics, image processing, medical informatics, complex diagnosis–therapy combinations, advanced skills and safety, and the 15-EC Clinical Technology Research project. The live programme page states that medicine and technology are interwoven in most courses and that students learn clinical skills and encounter practice through a clinical placement.
exception.ucrCourseEvidence: Reviewed all 151 current enriched UCR workbook rows, including descriptions, outline-derived profiles, disciplines, topics, methods, prerequisites and planned Fall 2026 cohort terms. HCBGATE101 Foundation of Life, Health & Biomedicine, HCBBIOM211 Functional Anatomy, HCBLIFE212 Human Physiology, HCBLIFE213 Biochemistry, HCBLIFE214 Life Science Laboratory, HCBLIFE311 Molecular Pathology & Genetics, HCBBIOM311 Pharmacology, HCBBIOM312 Infection & Immunity and HCBBIOM313 Mechanisms of Disease provide substantial biomedical foundations. DISGATE102 Mathematical Methods, DISMATH214 Advanced Calculus, DISMATH312 Linear Systems and DISMATH314 Probability & Statistics support quantitative work. DISGATE101 Introduction to Programming, DISDATA211 Machine Learning, DISDATA212 Image Processing & Computer Vision, DISDATA312 Robotics and related data courses support computation and medical-image applications. HCBCOGN112 Neurobiology, HCBCOGN212 Perception & Action, HCBBIOM111 Epidemiology & Public Health and GOSPHIL212 Ethics add relevant biological, population-health and ethical perspectives. The workbook nevertheless contains no thermodynamics or waves sequence for medicine, biomechanics sequence, biomedical instrumentation, physiological signal-acquisition laboratory, medical-device engineering, intensive-care technology, clinical simulation, patient examination or procedural-skills training, clinical safety qualification, supervised healthcare placement, integrated diagnosis–therapy course, or clinical-technology capstone. HCBPSYC312 Psychodiagnostics & Psychotherapies develops psychology-specific assessment and therapeutic competencies, not the medical procedures and technology practice required here. The available biomedical, mathematical and computational courses remain separate liberal-arts offerings rather than the target programme's integrated clinical-engineering formation.
